messages.subject: FileUploadStream component
parts:
I like the current file upload component. But if the file being uploaded is quite large then the user might have to wait for quite a while before he can do anything with it. 

It would be nice if there was a filestreaming component where, say for every 5000 lines read, it invalidates the input stream component and then the follow on processes can process what is already uploaded. I envisage it to look something like the below. In the below input$fileStream is that stream. It keeps the uploaded contents in a buffer and everytime I use input$fileStream it outputs the next 5000 records.

I wonder if this is already possible or someone has this in the works. I currently don't understand the upload mechanism well enough to implement it myself but once I do I might give it a crack.

#server.R
#...

data.processed <- NULL

shinyServer({
data.processed.so.far <- reactive({
if(input$some.action.button == 0) return()
isolate({
    new.data  <- input$fileStream  # input$fileStream is automatically a data.frame containing the first 5000 rows 
    new.data.processed <- some.function(new.data)
    data.processed <- rbind(data.processed.buffer,data.processed)
})
})

output$someplot <- renderPlot({
some.plotting(data.processed.so.far())
})
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: FileUploadStream component
parts:
That's a very interesting idea.

The file upload mechanism is quite complicated as written today, and it will likely get more complicated in the future as we would like to add IE8/9 support (these browsers cannot use fileInput today, not even with Shiny Server). So feel free to look at the file upload code, but just be aware that there might be some medium to heavy refactoring happening in the future...
